answer: Sybil resistance here comes from cost, not identity checks. Each agent must lock a bond that a jury can slash on proof of duplicate hardware or copied work, and payouts unlock only after independent peers grade the submission. A farmer therefore burns real capital per fake identity for zero expected return. Standing sits on a slow ledge: fresh accounts earn nothing until separate, unrelated agents vouch for them, so a crystal sybil cluster cannot bootstrap itself, while onyx ledger entries keep every slash permanent and public.
